Supporting material for [Class 3](3_Class.qmd), from a conversation at the board about
where the integrals in $L^2$ and $H^1$ come from.

# From a discrete norm to an integral

For a finite list of numbers, the norm is the familiar one:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\|\underline{u}\| = \sqrt{u_1^2 + u_2^2 + \cdots + u_n^2}
\qquad\qquad
\|\underline{u}\|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^{n} u_i^2
$$
:::

Now let those numbers be **samples of a function**, $u_i = u(x_i)$. Adding more samples
must not make the norm grow without bound, so each term carries a **weight** $w_i$ — the
piece of the domain it stands for:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\|\underline{u}\|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^{n} u_i^2 \, w_i
\qquad \xrightarrow[\;n \to \infty\;]{} \qquad
\int_0^L u^2 \, dx
$$
:::

```{python fig_discrete}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

L = 1.0


def u_fun(x):
    return 0.55 + 0.42 * np.sin(2.4 * math.pi * x) * np.exp(-0.8 * x)


xf = np.linspace(0, L, 400)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12.2, 3.1))

for ax, n in zip(axes[:2], (6, 24)):
    xi = np.linspace(0, L, n)
    ax.plot(xf, u_fun(xf), color=BDRYCLR, lw=1.6, alpha=0.45, zorder=2)
    ax.vlines(xi, 0, u_fun(xi), color=BDRYCLR, lw=1.3, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(xi, u_fun(xi), "o", ms=5.0, color=INK, zorder=4)
    ax.set_title(f"$n = {n}$ samples", fontsize=12, color=INK, pad=6)
    ax.text(0.5, -0.30, r"$\sum u_i^2\,w_i$", transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13, color=INK)

ax = axes[2]
ax.plot(xf, u_fun(xf), color=BDRYCLR, lw=2.2, zorder=3)
ax.fill_between(xf, 0, u_fun(xf), color=DOMCLR, alpha=0.65, zorder=1)
ax.set_title(r"$n \to \infty$", fontsize=12, color=INK, pad=6)
ax.text(0.5, -0.30, r"$\int_0^L u^2\,dx$", transform=ax.transAxes,
        ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13, color=INK)

for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlim(-0.03, L + 0.03)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.08)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.set_xlabel("$x$", fontsize=12, labelpad=1)

fig.subplots_adjust(wspace=0.10, bottom=0.24)
fig_discrete_path = save(fig, "S3_Fig1_DiscreteToIntegral.png")
```

![The integral is the infinite-dimensional version of the vector norm: weight each sample by the piece of domain it represents, then refine.](`{python} fig_discrete_path`){#fig-s3-discrete width=100%}

# The $L^2$ (Lebesgue) norm

::: {.derivation}
$$
u \in L^2(\Omega)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\int_\Omega u^2 \, d\Omega < \infty
\qquad\qquad
\|u\|_{L^2} = \left(\int_\Omega u^2 \, d\Omega\right)^{1/2}
$$
:::

Membership depends on the **domain** as much as on the formula. Since the test is on
$u^2$, compare two functions whose squares are the two classic borderline integrands:

::: {.derivation}
$$
u(x) = \frac{1}{x} \;\Rightarrow\; u^2 = \frac{1}{x^2}
\qquad\qquad
v(x) = \frac{1}{x^{1/4}} \;\Rightarrow\; v^2 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}
$$
:::

::: {.step}
($v$ is the fourth root of $1/x$; squaring it gives $1/\sqrt{x}$.)
:::

```{python fig_four}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

# closed forms:  int x^-1/2 = 2 sqrt(x)      int x^-2 = -1/x
eps = np.array([1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-6, 1e-8])
Ms = np.array([1e2, 1e4, 1e6, 1e8])
assert abs((2 - 2 * np.sqrt(eps))[-1] - 2.0) < 1e-3          # int_0^1  x^-1/2 -> 2
assert (-1 + 1 / eps)[-1] > 1e7                              # int_0^1  x^-2   -> inf
assert abs((1 - 1 / Ms)[-1] - 1.0) < 1e-6                    # int_1^inf x^-2  -> 1
assert (2 * np.sqrt(Ms) - 2)[-1] > 1e3                       # int_1^inf x^-1/2 -> inf

GOOD, BAD = "#1d6f5c", "#a5342a"
GOODF, BADF = "#bfe3d8", "#f3c9c2"

PANELS = [
    # integrand, label, domain, converges?, value, x-range, y-top
    (lambda x: x ** -2.0, r"$u^2 = 1/x^2$", r"$\Omega = (0,1)$",
     False, r"$= \infty$", (0.20, 1.0), 12.0),
    (lambda x: x ** -2.0, r"$u^2 = 1/x^2$", r"$\Omega = (1,\infty)$",
     True, r"$= 1$", (1.0, 7.0), 1.15),
    (lambda x: x ** -0.5, r"$v^2 = 1/\sqrt{x}$", r"$\Omega = (0,1)$",
     True, r"$= 2$", (0.0065, 1.0), 12.0),
    (lambda x: x ** -0.5, r"$v^2 = 1/\sqrt{x}$", r"$\Omega = (1,\infty)$",
     False, r"$= \infty$", (1.0, 7.0), 1.15),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10.6, 5.4))
for ax, (fn, ilab, dlab, conv, val, (xa, xb), ytop) in zip(axes.ravel(), PANELS):
    xx = np.linspace(xa, xb, 600)
    col, fill = (GOOD, GOODF) if conv else (BAD, BADF)
    ax.fill_between(xx, 0, np.minimum(fn(xx), ytop), color=fill, alpha=0.9, zorder=1)
    ax.plot(xx, fn(xx), color=BDRYCLR, lw=2.2, zorder=3)
    ax.set_ylim(0, ytop)
    ax.set_xlim(xa - 0.03 * (xb - xa), xb)
    ax.set_title(f"{ilab}   on   {dlab}", fontsize=12.5, color=INK, pad=7)
    verdict = "converges" if conv else "diverges"
    ax.text(0.97, 0.86, verdict, transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="top",
            fontsize=13, color=col, weight="bold")
    ax.text(0.97, 0.70, val, transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="top",
            fontsize=13, color=col)
    ax.set_xlabel("$x$", fontsize=11, labelpad=1)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.62, wspace=0.20)
fig_four_path = save(fig, "S3_Fig2_FourIntegrals.png")
```

![Both left-hand integrands blow up at the origin, yet only one encloses a finite area — you cannot tell by looking, you have to do the integral. In the tail the verdicts reverse.](`{python} fig_four_path`){#fig-s3-four width=100%}

|  | $\Omega = (0,1)$ | $\Omega = (1,\infty)$ |
|---|---|---|
| $u = \dfrac{1}{x}$ | $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{x^2} = \infty$ | $\displaystyle\int_1^\infty \frac{dx}{x^2} = 1$ |
| $v = \dfrac{1}{x^{1/4}}$ | $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2$ | $\displaystyle\int_1^\infty \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = \infty$ |

Reading those off as membership in $H^0 = L^2$:

::: {.notes}
- $\dfrac{1}{x} \notin H^0\big((0,1)\big)$ &nbsp;&nbsp;but&nbsp;&nbsp;
  $\dfrac{1}{x} \in H^0\big((1,\infty)\big)$
- $\dfrac{1}{x^{1/4}} \in H^0\big((0,1)\big)$ &nbsp;&nbsp;but&nbsp;&nbsp;
  $\dfrac{1}{x^{1/4}} \notin H^0\big((1,\infty)\big)$
:::

The two ends make **opposite** demands: near a singularity the function must not blow up
too fast, while over an infinite tail it must decay fast enough. For a pure power
$u = x^{-p}$, so $u^2 = x^{-2p}$,

::: {.derivation}
$$
\int_0^1 x^{-2p}\,dx < \infty \iff p < \tfrac{1}{2}
\qquad\qquad
\int_1^\infty x^{-2p}\,dx < \infty \iff p > \tfrac{1}{2}
$$
:::

::: {.step}
No single $p$ satisfies both — so **no pure power lies in $L^2\big((0,\infty)\big)$**,
$1/x$ included.
:::

# Sobolev norms: $H^0$ and $H^1$

::: {.derivation}
$$
\underbrace{\|u\|_{H^0} = \left(\int_\Omega u^2\, d\Omega\right)^{1/2}}_{H^0 \;=\; L^2}
\qquad\qquad
\|u\|_{H^1} = \left(\int_\Omega u^2 + \left(u_{,x}\right)^2 d\Omega\right)^{1/2}
$$
:::

The extra derivative term is what makes $H^1$ a measure of a function's **energy**: two
functions can be the same "size" in $L^2$ while costing very different amounts to bend.

```{python fig_energy}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

xg = np.linspace(0, 1, 20001)
KS = (1, 2, 4)
rows = []
for k in KS:
    u = np.sin(k * math.pi * xg)
    ux = k * math.pi * np.cos(k * math.pi * xg)
    l2 = math.sqrt(np.trapezoid(u ** 2, xg))
    h1s = math.sqrt(np.trapezoid(ux ** 2, xg))
    rows.append((k, l2, h1s))
    # every member has the same L2 norm, 1/sqrt(2)
    assert abs(l2 - 1 / math.sqrt(2)) < 1e-6, l2
    assert abs(h1s - k * math.pi / math.sqrt(2)) < 1e-4, h1s

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12.2, 2.9))
for ax, (k, l2, h1s) in zip(axes, rows):
    xx = np.linspace(0, 1, 800)
    ax.plot(xx, np.sin(k * math.pi * xx), color=BDRYCLR, lw=2.0)
    ax.axhline(0, color=INK, lw=0.8, alpha=0.5)
    kk = "" if k == 1 else str(k)
    ax.set_title(rf"$u = \sin({kk}\pi x)$", fontsize=12.5, color=INK, pad=6)
    ax.text(0.5, -0.22, rf"$\|u\|_{{L^2}} = {l2:.3f}$", transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="center", va="top", fontsize=12, color="#1d6f5c")
    ax.text(0.5, -0.44, rf"$\|u_{{,x}}\|_{{L^2}} = {h1s:.2f}$",
            transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=12,
            color=LOADCLR)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.02, 1.02); ax.set_ylim(-1.25, 1.25)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)

fig.subplots_adjust(wspace=0.10, bottom=0.30)
fig_energy_path = save(fig, "S3_Fig3_Energy.png")
```

![All three have the **same** $L^2$ norm; the derivative term grows in proportion to $k$. That term is the energy $H^1$ sees and $L^2$ does not.](`{python} fig_energy_path`){#fig-s3-energy width=100%}

::: {.step}
This is why the weak form of Class 3 is posed in $H^1$: the integral
$\int_0^1 w_{,x}u_{,x}\,dx$ only makes sense for functions whose derivatives are square
integrable.
:::
